skill.name: Microsoft Graph API
skill.description: Access Microsoft 365 email and Outlook calendar data through Microsoft Graph scripts with device-code authentication.
skill.summary: Read, search, send email and manage Outlook calendar events through Microsoft Graph.
skill.author: BLTGV

security_audit.summary: The scanner reported many static hits, but most external-command and reconnaissance detections are false positives from TypeScript template literals, Markdown code fences, or usage examples. Confirmed risks remain around authenticated Microsoft Graph network access, email sending, calendar writes, and plaintext local storage of OAuth credentials. No prompt-injection attempt was found in the reviewed files.

remediation.issue: OAuth access and refresh tokens are stored in a local JSON credentials file.
remediation.suggestion: Use an operating-system credential store or encrypt the file, restrict file permissions, and document token revocation steps.

remediation.issue: The skill can send email and create calendar events as the authenticated user.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation before every side-effecting command and show recipients, attendees, subject, time, and body before execution.

remediation.issue: The default public Graph client id may not satisfy tenant governance requirements.
remediation.suggestion: Encourage or require a tenant-owned Azure app registration and request only the Graph scopes needed for each command.

remediation.issue: Sensitive email and calendar content can be passed through command-line arguments.
remediation.suggestion: Support stdin or restricted temporary files for message bodies and event descriptions to reduce process-list and shell-history exposure.

remediation.issue: Microsoft Graph requests do not implement automatic pagination or rate-limit retry.
remediation.suggestion: Add bounded pagination and Retry-After handling so users do not repeat broad requests manually.

semantic_findings.title: High-Impact Microsoft 365 Account Actions
semantic_findings.description: The skill can send mail and create calendar events through authenticated Microsoft Graph calls. These actions can affect recipients and calendars if an agent runs them without clear user approval.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The documentation advertises email and calendar write actions, and the code directly calls sendMail and event creation endpoints. This is intended behavior, but it is a real high-impact account capability.

semantic_findings.title: Default Public OAuth Client With Broad Delegated Scopes
semantic_findings.description: The code defaults to a public Microsoft Graph client id and declares mail read, mail send, calendar read, and calendar write scopes. Tenant-owned app registration and least-privilege consent are safer for organizations.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The scope declarations and default client id are explicit in the inspected files. The risk depends on tenant policy, so confidence is high for capability and medium for impact.

semantic_findings.title: Sensitive Message Data Passed Through CLI Arguments
semantic_findings.description: Examples and option parsing pass email recipients, subjects, body text, calendar attendees, and event body as command arguments. These values can appear in shell history, process listings, or agent logs.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The CLI options and documented send examples place message and event contents in arguments. Exposure depends on the runtime environment, but the data path is clear.

content.user_title: Connect Microsoft Graph Email and Calendar
content.value_statement: Microsoft 365 email and calendar work often requires switching tools and copying data manually. This skill lets an AI assistant use Microsoft Graph scripts for authenticated Outlook mail and calendar tasks.
actual_capabilities: Lists, reads, and searches Outlook email through Microsoft Graph.
Sends email with to, cc, bcc, subject, body, and optional HTML content.
Lists, views, and searches Outlook calendar events by date range or query.
Creates calendar events with location, body, attendees, and all-day settings.
Supports device-code authentication, token refresh, and named credential profiles.
Returns structured status output for success, errors, and authentication states.
limitations: Requires Bun, network access, and a Microsoft account with approved Graph permissions.
Stores OAuth credentials in a local JSON file under the user home directory.
Does not implement attachment download, pagination beyond top limits, or automatic rate-limit retry.
Side-effect actions such as sending mail and creating events require careful user confirmation.

best_practices: Use named profiles to separate work, personal, and tenant-specific Microsoft accounts.
Ask for explicit confirmation before sending email or creating calendar events.
Use the smallest Graph permission scope needed for the current task.
anti_patterns: Do not send email or create events from inferred intent alone.
Do not paste sensitive message bodies into shared prompts or logs.
Do not reuse a broad default OAuth app when tenant policy requires a dedicated app registration.

faq.question: What Microsoft services does this skill use?
faq.answer: It uses Microsoft Graph for Outlook mail, Outlook calendar, and Microsoft account profile authentication.

faq.question: How does authentication work?
faq.answer: The scripts use Microsoft device-code authentication and store refreshed credentials for later commands.

faq.question: Can it send email?
faq.answer: Yes. It can send email after authentication with Mail.Send permission and user approval.

faq.question: Can it create calendar events?
faq.answer: Yes. It can create events with subject, start time, end time, location, description, attendees, and all-day settings.

faq.question: Where are credentials stored?
faq.answer: Credentials are stored locally in a JSON file under ~/.config/api-skills in the user home directory.

faq.question: Does it handle attachments?
faq.answer: No. The current scripts expose message metadata, body content, folders, email sending, and calendar operations.
